title: To live, to get up, to run
topic: the present tense of verbs with the vowel a (גָּר, קָם, רָץ)
why: Second lesson on the present tense: short verbs like גָּר (to live), which have only two consonants and the vowel a, with a feminine in -a. You use them to talk about your home and your day, reusing the four forms from the previous lesson.

{"lessons": ["

Verbs with two consonants

You already know אֵיפֹה אַתָּה גָּר? (where do you live?). גָּר belongs to a family of very short verbs: two consonants and the vowel a. Their root actually has three letters (ג־ו־ר), but the middle ו disappears in the present.

Three verbs from this family: גָּר (to live), קָם (to get up), רָץ (to run).

m. sg.f. sg.m. pl.f. pl.
גָּר
gar		גָּרָה
gara		גָּרִים
garim		גָּרוֹת
garot
קָם
kam		קָמָה
kama		קָמִים
kamim		קָמוֹת
kamot
רָץ
rats		רָצָה
ratsa		רָצִים
ratsim		רָצוֹת
ratsot

Four forms, always by gender and number. In the plural, nothing new: -im and -ot.

The trap: here the feminine ends in -a (גָּרָה, gara), not in -et like כּוֹתֶבֶת.

", "

Coming and putting

Two more very useful short verbs: בָּא (to come, to arrive) and שָׂם (to put, to place). In בָּאָה, both א are silent: ba-a. שָׂם is written with שׂ (dot on the left), which is read s.

m. sg.f. sg.m. pl.f. pl.
בָּא
ba		בָּאָה
ba'a		בָּאִים
ba'im		בָּאוֹת
ba'ot
שָׂם
sam		שָׂמָה
sama		שָׂמִים
samim		שָׂמוֹת
samot
הוּא בָּא מִתֵּל אָבִיב.He's coming from Tel Aviv. [hu ba mi-tel aviv]
הִיא שָׂמָה סֵפֶר עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן.She puts a book on the table. [hi sama sefer al ha-shulkhan]

בָּא means both \"to come\" and \"to arrive\": אַבָּא בָּא! (Dad's here!). With הַבַּיְתָה (toward home), it means \"to come home\": אֲנִי בָּא הַבַּיְתָה, I'm coming home.

", "

My home, my day

אֲנַחְנוּ גָּרִים בְּדִירָה קְטַנָּה.We live in a small apartment. [anakhnu garim be-dira ktana]
יֵשׁ חֶדֶר, מִטְבָּח וּמִרְפֶּסֶת.There's a room, a kitchen and a balcony. [yesh kheder, mitbakh u-mirpeset]
אֲנִי קָם מֻקְדָּם בַּבֹּקֶר.I get up early in the morning (a man speaking). [ani kam mukdam ba-boker]
דָּנָה רָצָה בַּפַּארְק.Dana runs in the park. [Dana ratsa ba-park]
בָּעֶרֶב הֵם בָּאִים הַבַּיְתָה.In the evening, they come home. [ba-erev hem ba'im ha-bayta]

In Israel, almost everyone lives in an apartment, and the מִרְפֶּסֶת (balcony) is the favorite room: people have their coffee there and eat dinner there in summer.

English says \"I get up\" with two words; Hebrew uses a single short verb: אֲנִי קָם.
